title: Snow, Boulevard de Clichy, Paris

image.credit: Minneapolis Institute of Art; via arthistoryproject.com

altText: A snowy street scene on a wide Paris boulevard, painted in soft whites, greys, and muted colors. The city looks quiet and cold, with buildings lining the street.

source.verifiedBy: arthistoryproject.com artwork page text (title, year, medium, collection, public-domain statement)

context: An oil painting by Paul Signac, a French painter, made in 1886. The source page tags it Landscape Painting. Signac is known as a painter who used small touches of color, and a city street under snow gave him a chance to study many shades of white and grey.

descriptions.k: It snowed in Paris! Look at the street. It is wide and covered in snow. The sky is grey and the air feels cold. Can you find the buildings? What would you do in the snow?
descriptions.g12: Paul Signac painted a snowy street in Paris, France. He used many whites and greys, and some soft colors too. The city looks quiet and cold. What colors do you see in the snow? How does the painting make you feel?
descriptions.g35: Paul Signac painted Snow, Boulevard de Clichy, Paris in 1886 in France. A boulevard is a wide city street. The snow is not just white. Signac used many shades of white, grey, and soft color. Look at the street, the buildings, and the sky. How does he make a cold winter day feel real?
descriptions.g68: In Snow, Boulevard de Clichy, Paris (1886), Signac paints a city street under snow using a range of whites, greys, and muted colors. The wide boulevard and buildings create depth. Snow can be quiet and bright at once. How do color and composition create the sense of a winter day in the city, and what mood do they suggest?
descriptions.g910: Signac's Snow, Boulevard de Clichy, Paris (1886) studies a winter city through subtle shifts of tone and color. The recession of the boulevard organizes the space while snow softens edges. As a young Parisian painter, Signac was interested in how color works. How does the painting turn a plain, cold scene into a study of atmosphere, and what feelings does it evoke?
descriptions.g1112: Snow, Boulevard de Clichy, Paris (1886) shows Signac, a French painter linked to the generation after Impressionism, treating a wintry city scene as a study of color and atmosphere. The painting's handling of whites and greys asks whether snow is a lack of color or a field of many. How do tone, brushwork, and spatial structure shape your sense of urban winter, and how might others read it differently?

teacherNote.context: An 1886 oil painting by Paul Signac of a snowy street in Paris. The source page tags it Landscape Painting. Signac is associated with the generation of French painters after Impressionism.
directions: Ask students to list as many colors as they can find in the snow, then try mixing them with paint.
Compare this with a photograph of a snowy street and discuss what the painter emphasizes.
Discuss how weather can change the mood of a place in art.
